Stack QTL summary tables from multiple fitted models

Source: R/aimTable.R
aimTable.Rd

Combines the summary() output from two or more qtlAim or gwasAim objects into a single stacked data.frame with a leading Trait column, ready for export to a spreadsheet or a LaTeX table via xtable.

Usage

aimTable(..., genObj = NULL, labels = NULL, columns = "all", LOD = TRUE)

Arguments

...

One or more fitted objects of class "qtlAim" or "gwasAim".

genObj

The genomic data object required by summary(): a "wgCross" produced by primeCross (for qtlAim objects) or a "wgPanel" produced by primePanel (for gwasAim objects). Supply a single shared object when all models used the same genomic data, or a list of objects with one element per model in ....

labels

Optional character vector of trait labels, one per model in .... If NULL (default), the left-hand side of the fixed component of each model's call is used.

columns

Either "all" (default) to include every column returned by summary(), or a numeric vector of column indices to retain (applied after the leading Trait column is inserted, so column 1 in summary() output corresponds to columns = 1).

LOD

Logical; passed through to summary.qtlAim() / summary.gwasAim(). If TRUE (default), a LOD score column is appended.

Value

A data.frame of class c("aimTable", "data.frame") with a leading Trait column followed by the columns from the individual summary() tables. Rows with no detected QTL are excluded. The attribute "obj.class" records the common object class ("qtlAim" or "gwasAim").

Details

All objects supplied via ... must satisfy two rules: (1) they must all be of the same class (all qtlAim or all gwasAim; mixing is not permitted); and (2) for qtlAim objects, all models must have been run with the same gen.type (all "interval" or all "marker"), ensuring a consistent column layout in the stacked table. Objects for which no QTL / significant markers were detected are silently dropped from the result with a console message.

See also

qtlAim, gwasAim, summary.qtlAim, summary.gwasAim

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
## Two QTL models sharing the same cross object
gw.qtl  <- qtlAim(gw.asf,  genObj = genoObj, merge.by = "Genotype")
yld.qtl <- qtlAim(yld.asf, genObj = genoObj, merge.by = "Genotype")

at <- aimTable(gw.qtl, yld.qtl,
               genObj = genoObj,
               labels = c("Grain weight", "Yield"))
print(at)

## Export to LaTeX (requires xtable)
# print(xtable::xtable(at), include.rownames = FALSE)

## Two GWAS models
gw.gwas  <- gwasAim(gw.asf,  genObj = panelObj, merge.by = "Genotype")
yld.gwas <- gwasAim(yld.asf, genObj = panelObj, merge.by = "Genotype")

at2 <- aimTable(gw.gwas, yld.gwas, genObj = panelObj)
print(at2)
} # }
